summary: Horizon has 13 doctors, bilingual pages, WhatsApp and Google reviews. A few visible errors and conflicting numbers make a new patient hesitate right before booking.

findings.problem: A stray No results line appears at the top of the page above the header, and one review card shows a raw screenshot file name.
findings.cost: Visible leftovers make a clinic look unfinished at the first glance, before the patient reads anything.
findings.fix: A clean page with no leftover or system text.

findings.problem: The hero says +870 trusted customers while the counter says +23000. A reviewer names Dr. Selena, who is not on the staff list, and Dr. Omar appears under two spellings.
findings.cost: Conflicting numbers make patients doubt every claim on the page.
findings.fix: One verified set of numbers and a staff list that matches your reviews.

findings.problem: Seven doctors share the same generic image and several others share a Female Dentist placeholder.
findings.cost: Patients choose who treats them. Without real photos, 13 doctors look like none.
findings.fix: Real doctor profiles with photos, specialty and credentials.

findings.problem: There is no booking form on the homepage. Visitors must leave to book, and no before and after results or review count appear.
findings.cost: Every extra click costs bookings, and unproven claims such as best price and world class do not persuade.
findings.fix: A booking form in the hero, a review count and captioned before and after cases.

redesign: A proof first homepage with real doctor photos, a review count and captioned smile cases beside every booking button.
A booking form in the hero plus WhatsApp, so a patient books in under 30 seconds.
Treatment pages in Arabic and English written to rank for searches like dental implants Riyadh.
